target.name: folic acid metabolic process
target.description: Folic acid metabolism supplies the one-carbon units that cells need to make purines, thymidylate and methionine, so it sits upstream of DNA replication, repair and methylation. Dietary folate must first be taken up and retained: a high-affinity receptor and the reduced folate and proton-coupled intestinal transporters bring it into cells, a mitochondrial carrier moves it across the inner membrane, and polyglutamylation traps it intracellularly.

target.name: positive regulation of actin filament depolymerization
target.description: Actin filaments must be taken apart as fast as they are built, and this is the regulatory arm that accelerates filament depolymerization to recycle subunits back into the polymerizable pool. Without it, cells cannot retract a lamellipodium, turn over adhesions, or remodel the cortex, so migration, cytokinesis and neuronal process dynamics stall.

target.name: maternal process involved in parturition
target.description: Birth requires coordinated changes in the mother's uterus, and this maternal contribution to parturition covers the signals that convert a quiescent, pregnancy-sustaining myometrium into a synchronously contracting muscle that expels the fetus and placenta. Its timing sets the boundary between preterm labour and term delivery, and failure of the contractile switch produces prolonged or obstructed labour and postpartum haemorrhage.

target.name: AKT phosphorylates targets in the nucleus
target.description: Growth factor and insulin signalling ends in changes to gene expression, and one route is activated AKT entering the nucleus to phosphorylate transcription factors there. This is how a cell converts a survival or nutrient signal into a decision not to die: AKT phosphorylation of the forkhead factors FOXO1, FOXO3, FOXO4 and FOXO6 blocks their activity, driving them out of the nucleus and silencing the apoptotic, cell-cycle-arrest and stress-resistance genes they otherwise switch on.
